mission: Make the ops runbook workflows dispatchable (follow-up to PR #139): the default branch main does not carry ops-readonly.yml/ops-write.yml, so workflow_dispatch returned 404. A push to staging that changes either file registers it; every job is skipped on that push. Staging only; no collector, setting, price, identity, Market Value/Index, secret or Railway change; no deploy, enqueue or runbook run in this PR.

impacts.reason: Adds a push trigger limited to staging and to the workflow's own file, and gates every job on github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch', so the push run only registers the workflow and runs nothing (no environment, no secret). ops-write's registration run uses its own concurrency group so it never displaces a run waiting for owner approval. Dispatch behaviour, inputs, gates and credentials are unchanged.
Asserts the push trigger is limited to staging and the workflow's own path, and that every job is gated on workflow_dispatch.
Explains registration and what a 404 on dispatch means.

resources.name: GitHub Actions: ops-readonly and ops-write workflows (registration push trigger only)

dependencies: ops workflows from PR #139 (unchanged dispatch path)
impact.deployment_impact: Workflow, test and doc only. collector_services is empty and no raw_dependency_migration: 0 collector rollouts, no DDL. No path under services/, packages/ or apps/ changes. The merge push starts one ops-readonly and one ops-write run whose jobs are all skipped.

recovery.procedure: Native revert of this PR removes the push trigger; the workflows then stay registered but unchanged otherwise. No data, schema, provider or service configuration to undo.
recovery.trigger: Any ops job running on a push event, or a dispatch still returning 404 after the registration run.
recovery.backup: Not applicable: no schema or row change. Railway Postgres daily backups continue.

verification.observation_window: After merge: the registration runs show all jobs skipped; one ops-readonly staging-state run and one official-images-status run succeed with read-only sessions, and their summaries are attached to PR #139.
